title: Psalms Bible Quiz - Chapter 123
description: Ten questions on Psalms 123: eyes lifted to Yahweh like servants looking to their master's hand, with a plea for mercy amid contempt.

questions.text: What does the psalmist lift up to God in verse 1?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:1 says "I lift up my eyes to you, you who sit in the heavens."

questions.text: How does the psalmist describe the one to whom he lifts his eyes?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:1 says "you who sit in the heavens."

answers.text: You who sit in the heavens
You who ride on the clouds of the sky

questions.text: To what do the eyes of servants look, according to verse 2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:2 says "the eyes of servants look to the hand of their master."

questions.text: To whose hand do the eyes of a maid look?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:2 says "as the eyes of a maid to the hand of her mistress."

questions.text: To whom do "our eyes" look in verse 2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:2 says "so our eyes look to Yahweh, our God."

questions.text: Until when do "our eyes" look to Yahweh?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:2 says our eyes look to Yahweh, our God, until he has mercy on us.

answers.text: Until he has mercy on us
Until the rain falls on the land

questions.text: Which request is repeated in verse 3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:3 says "Have mercy on us, Yahweh, have mercy on us."

questions.text: Why do they ask for mercy in verse 3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:3 says "for we have endured much contempt."

answers.text: They have lost a great battle

questions.text: Whose scoffing fills their soul, according to verse 4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:4 says their soul is exceedingly filled with the scoffing of those who are at ease.

answers.text: The young men of the city

questions.text: Whose contempt is mentioned at the end of the psalm?
questions.explanation: Psalms 123:4 ends with "the contempt of the proud."
